text.title: Regression Test First Bugfix Workflow Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules every Regression Test First Bugfix Workflow application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: `red_test.commit` MUST be an ancestor of every commit that touches production code in the fix PR (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <red_test.commit> <first-fix-commit>` succeeds), and the commit message MUST contain the alert URL. The CI run for that commit MUST show the new test failing. A PR whose first commit already contains the fix, or whose test commit follows the fix commit, fails this rule regardless of the final green run.
rule.rationale: A test written after the fix has never been observed to fail, so nobody knows whether it detects the bug or merely passes. The commit order is the only durable evidence that the red state existed; "I ran it locally and it failed" is not reviewable a month later when the same alert fires again.

rule.statement: The red test MUST fail with the same observable outcome the alert reports: the same exception type and message fragment, or the same wrong output value. `red_test.asserts[]` MUST contain at least one assertion on that outcome and, where the bug had a side effect (a row written, an email sent, a charge made), at least one assertion that the side effect is absent. A test that asserts `pytest.raises(Exception)` or only that "something failed" is rejected.

rationale.source: Kent Beck, 'Test-Driven Development: By Example' (2002); widely established practice in test engineering

rule.rationale: A test that fails for the wrong reason (an import error, a fixture typo) goes red, the fix goes in, the test goes green because the typo was fixed, and the bug ships with a passing regression test named after it. The side-effect assertion is what catches the checkout that now returns 422 but still creates the order.

rule.statement: The test's inputs MUST be taken from the alert payload (request body, query parameters, locale, timezone, feature-flag state, record ids) and recorded in the workflow record; personal data is replaced field-by-field with values of the same shape, and the substitution is noted. Inputs invented from the developer's guess about the cause are forbidden until the payload-derived test reproduces the failure.

rationale.source: Sentry documentation on event payloads and breadcrumbs; widely established practice in production debugging

rule.rationale: The checkout bug that only fires with `locale=tr_TR` and `amount=0.0` is not reproduced by a test with `en_US` and `9.99`. The payload is the one artefact that is known to trigger the fault; a test built from a hypothesis proves the hypothesis, not the bug.

rule.statement: `red_test.path` MUST be under `tests/regression/` (or the runner's equivalent regression directory) and named after the alert slug, with the alert id in the test's docstring or leading comment. The test MUST NOT perform real network calls, read the wall clock or use unseeded randomness; time is frozen and external calls are stubbed. A test that passes and fails across three consecutive runs of the same commit is rejected.
rule.rationale: A flaky regression test is worse than none: the team learns to retry it, then to skip it, and the bug it guarded returns silently. Locating it under a regression directory with the alert id is what lets the next developer, or the next incident review, find every test that exists because production once broke.

rule.statement: The fix commit MUST change only what is needed to turn the red test green; `fix.diff_lines` is recorded and refactors go in a separate PR. The fix PR MUST NOT modify the assertions of the red test; if an assertion was wrong, the change to it is a separate commit with its own explanation, and the test MUST be shown failing again on the fix's parent after the assertion change.

rationale.source: Kent Beck, 'Test-Driven Development: By Example' (2002); Google Engineering Practices, 'Small CLs'

rule.rationale: The fastest way to make a red test green is to edit the assertion, and under SLA pressure it happens. Separating the assertion edit and re-proving red is the only guard. A fix mixed with a refactor cannot be reverted alone, and the reviewer cannot tell which of the 400 lines is the one that matters.

rule.statement: `verification.ci_run_url` MUST point to the CI run of the complete PR with `passed: true`, and the record MUST also cite the CI run of the test-only commit showing the failure. `passed` MUST be set from CI output, never from a local run. A PR merged with the regression test skipped, marked `xfail`, or excluded from the CI job fails this rule.

rationale.source: widely established practice in continuous integration

rule.rationale: Local runs share the developer's environment, cached fixtures and uncommitted files. The pair of CI runs is the reproducible statement "this test detects this bug and this fix removes it"; either run alone proves half of it.

rule.statement: When the SLA forces a ship-first hotfix, the workflow record MUST still be created with `red_test` marked pending, a follow-up ticket URL, and a due date at most 14 days after the hotfix merge. The alert MUST NOT be marked resolved in the alerting tool until the regression test is merged. A hotfix with no follow-up ticket, or with the alert already closed, fails this rule.

rationale.source: widely established practice in incident management

rule.rationale: The hotfix stops the bleeding; the test stops the recurrence. Teams that close the alert at hotfix time carry a growing set of bugs that were fixed once and guarded never, and each one comes back on the next refactor of the same code with nobody remembering the first time.

rule.statement: `review.next_review_at` MUST be set to the merge date plus 90 days. At that review the record MUST cite the alert's status in the alerting tool: no regression event for the same issue in the window, and no new issue with the same stack signature. A regression event within the window reopens the record and requires a new red test for the new inputs before any second fix.

rationale.source: Sentry documentation on issue resolution and regression detection

rule.rationale: Alerting tools flag an issue as regressed when a resolved error reappears, which is exactly the signal that the regression test did not cover the real input space. Checking it 90 days out, against the tool rather than memory, is the only way the workflow can learn which of its tests actually held.
